title: 3D-printed insole
subtitle: A thin sports insole printed in two materials
role: Product design, KeyShot renders and the print animation
summary: This is a thin 3D-printed sports insole made from two materials, PEBA and TPU, with an open heel that sits on top of the insole already inside a shoe. When I worked on it in 2025, I was doing a great deal of 3D printing and exploring how combining two materials could produce a specific function. It felt like another way of understanding function.

sections.heading: Function through material combination
sections.body:
Earlier projects had led me to think about function mostly through mechanisms and overall form. Here the work grew directly out of multi-material 3D printing. I wanted to study how two materials affect and support each other, how they connect functionally in one part, and what that pairing does biomechanically.

The insole is meant for sport and is not a medical corrective insert. Because it rests on top of the shoe's existing insole instead of replacing it, the heel stays open, adding structure under the arch and forefoot without lifting the heel.

sections.heading: Frame, body and animation
sections.body:
A firmer frame branches forward from the heel opening toward the forefoot, while a softer body fills the spaces between its arms. In the first concept, a green frame sat beneath a translucent shell with a dark oval pad at the forefoot. I rendered that version as a turntable in KeyShot and animated the print layer by layer in Blender.

In the later redesign, the green branching frame sits over a black body, with open windows where the frame crosses the arch and cream cushioned zones set into the top.

sections.heading: Learning through test prints
sections.body: Because this was design done as exploration, the form moved forward through printed parts. I started with small test sections, moved to half-length pieces, and then printed full-length insoles. Later prototypes shifted the softer body to a clear honeycomb lattice alongside the branching frame.
